summary: This diff adds two new files: a red-team report and a notes file for a session pricing cache design review. The report lists 12 findings (F1-F12) ranked Critical/High/Medium/Low against two nightmare scenarios: wrong prices and Redis cluster meltdown. Each finding has severity, explanation, fix direction, and a re-check step, ending in a checklist table and a note that three design changes (versioned keys, enumerating pricing inputs, dedicated cache instance) would clear most Critical/High findings. The notes file records interpretive assumptions: how 're-check' was defined, the severity scale's anchoring, no codebase/Redis access assumed, and that F8 could escalate to Critical under certain conditions.

claims.text: KEYS session:*:pricing blocks the whole Redis cluster including rate limiting and feature flags
claims.anchor: F1. `KEYS session:*:pricing` blocks the shared cluster

claims.text: Only invalidation trigger is promo_changed, so catalog/tax price changes serve stale data for up to 30 minutes
claims.anchor: F2. Catalog price and tax changes never invalidate the cache

claims.text: Cache key is session ID only and hash is written once, missing mid-session pricing-affecting changes (address, coupon, currency, cart)
claims.anchor: F3. Cache key ignores everything that changes pricing within a session

claims.text: 40KB x 200k sessions = ~8GB, exactly the stated free capacity, with no headroom for overhead/growth
claims.anchor: F4. Sizing has zero headroom on a shared cluster

claims.text: The cache_pricing_v1 kill switch flag is served from the same Redis cluster it is meant to protect against
claims.anchor: F5. Kill switch lives inside the failure it must stop

claims.text: "No circuit breaker needed" is wrong for slow Redis and for stampede scenarios
claims.anchor: F6. "No circuit breaker needed" is wrong for slow Redis and for stampedes

claims.text: Event-driven invalidation has a lost-event window and a write-after-delete race condition
claims.anchor: F7. Event-driven invalidation has a lost-event and a race window

claims.text: The doc does not specify whether the charge path uses the same price as the cached quote
Rollout plan of 5% for a day then 100% defines no gating metrics and is a 20x step with untested memory math above 5%
claims.anchor: F9. Rollout plan has no success criteria and a blunt ramp

claims.text: No observability exists for cache staleness or invalidation (hit/miss counter, cache-age histogram, invalidation-lag gauge, mismatch comparison)
claims.anchor: F10. No observability for staleness or invalidation

claims.text: 30-minute TTL versus session length relationship is unstated in the doc
claims.anchor: F11. 30-minute TTL vs. session length is unstated

claims.text: The key namespace session:{id}:pricing has no ownership/namespace convention within the shared cluster
claims.anchor: F12. Shared keyspace has no namespace or ownership convention

claims.text: Three design changes (versioned keys for F1+F7, enumerating pricing inputs for F2+F3, dedicated cache instance for F4+F5) would clear all five Criticals and most Highs
F8 would escalate from Medium to Critical if the charge path reprices independently of the quote
claims.anchor: user_notes.md: F8 (quote vs. charge price source) is rated Medium because the doc is silent

claims.text: No script was written for re-checks because the checks are judgments about a design doc rather than machine-checkable properties
claims.anchor: user_notes.md: A way to re-check them after I fix things

claims.text: Numbers cited (8GB, 200k sessions, 40KB) were taken at face value from the target doc with no independent verification
claims.anchor: user_notes.md: No codebase or Redis cluster access was assumed

risks.anchor: F4. Sizing has zero headroom on a shared cluster
risks.note: 40KB per session, 200k sessions, and 8GB free capacity are asserted without a source visible in this chunk; user_notes.md confirms these were taken at face value from the target doc, not independently verified.

risks.anchor: F1. `KEYS session:*:pricing` blocks the shared cluster
risks.note: The claim that this specific scan would trip client timeouts fleet-wide is argued from general Redis behavior, not from evidence in this chunk (no benchmark or log cited).

least_confident: Whether the severity ratings (e.g., F4 and F6 as High rather than Critical) reflect a consistent, defensible standard is hard to judge without seeing the original design doc these findings respond to.
